Jordan Love’s ability to manage the game and Christian Watson’s speed will test the Panthers’ secondary, which lacks proven playmakers in the back end. Carolina’s offense, led by Bryce Young, faces a Packers defense that ranks among the NFL’s best at stopping the run, though injuries to linebackers like Jaelan Phillips (out) and Bobby Okereke (questionable) could create gaps. The Packers’ offensive line, despite missing Travis Glover (out) and Sean Rhyan (out), still features Jordan Morgan and Aaron Banks, who should provide enough protection for Love to thrive. Special teams are evenly matched, but the Packers’ experience in high-stakes games gives them an edge. The Panthers’ best chance is forcing turnovers and exploiting the Packers’ injury-depleted defensive line, but Green Bay’s overall superiority should prevail. Final score: Green Bay Packers 24, Carolina Panthers 20.
